keyVerseText: Elkanah his son, and Ebiasaph his son, and Assir his son,
rootMeaning: The name אֶבְיָסָף (ʼEbyâçâph) is a contracted form of אֲבִיאָסָף (ʼĂbîyʼâçâph), meaning "my father has gathered." This root meaning combines the elements 'father' and 'to gather,' suggesting a sense of familial or ancestral gathering or unification. Beyond the English gloss, this implies a personal and communal dimension, emphasizing the gathering or preservation of family lineage or heritage.
usageInScripture: The word אֶבְיָסָף appears three times in Scripture, consistently referring to a descendant of Korah, an Israelite. Its translation as "of Ebiasaph" in two instances and "and Ebiasaph" in one indicates its use primarily as a proper name identifying a specific individual within a genealogical or narrative context. This consistency highlights the term's role in marking lineage and identity within the biblical record.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֶבְיָסָף as "my father has gathered" enriches our appreciation of biblical genealogy as more than mere record-keeping; it points to God's providential gathering and preservation of His people through generations. This name reflects the faithfulness of God in sustaining His covenant community, reminding believers that their spiritual heritage is secured by divine gathering. It underscores the continuity of God's plan through family lines and invites reflection on how God gathers His people into one spiritual family in Christ. Recognizing this deep-rooted meaning fosters trust in God's ongoing work to unite and preserve His church.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 6:23, the listing of Elkanah, Ebiasaph, and Assir as successive sons emphasizes the continuity of God's covenant people through generations. The name Ebiasaph, meaning "my father has gathered," enriches the verse by highlighting the divine activity behind this lineage—the gathering and sustaining of the family. This reminds readers that each generation is part of God's purposeful assembly, a truth that encourages faith in God's sovereign care over His people.
